title: Base change for a proper morphism, against an open immersion
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ and the scheme-base data of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and carry that ambient exceptional right adjoint datum. Let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g':X'\hookrightarrow X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], normalize $Rf^\times$ as the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ using the proper compactification $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ and the comparisons in the given datum. Then $Rf'_*$ admits the corresponding right adjoint $Rf'^\times$, and for every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the canonical comparison
$$\beta_K:Lg'^*Rf^\times K\longrightarrow Rf'^\times Lg^*K$$
is an isomorphism. To specify its normalization, write $\Gamma:g_!Rf'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*g'_!$ for the derived proper/open map induced on K-injective representatives by the sheaf map [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison]. The comparison $\beta_K$ is the $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$ transpose of the $g_!\dashv g^*$ transpose of
$$g_!Rf'_*g'^*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{\Gamma}Rf_*g'_!g'^*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}}Rf_*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f}K.$$
All open pullbacks here are exact, so $Lg^*=g^*$ and $Lg'^*=g'^*$.

Independently of this optional ambient datum, let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ with the coefficients of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], let $f$ be proper and $g$ an open immersion as above. For every bounded-below complex $K$ of etale origin [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], the analogous canonical comparison for the relative exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is an isomorphism:
$$g'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'^!g^*K.$$
Here the relative adjunction is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; no existence of the unrestricted pro-etale ambient datum is inferred from this clause [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge].

proof.text:
Let $c=(j,p)$ be the distinguished compactification of the ambient datum and $c_0$ its FullCD bound. Since $f$ is proper and $p$ is separated, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $j:X\to\overline X$ proper. Thus $j$ is a refinement $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)\to(j,p)$ in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The comparisons and their unit/counit equations in [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] identify the proper normalization $Rf_*$ with $Rp_*j_!$ and the given right adjoint with $Rf^\times$. For a module sheaf $F$, exactness of $j_!$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] and clause 1 of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] give
$$R^qf_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(j_!F[0]))=0\quad(q>c_0).$$
This bound applies to every pro-etale module sheaf, since FullCD in the assumed datum has exactly that quantifier.

proof.text: Properness is stable under base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], so $f'$ is proper; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $g'$ open. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison] to $(p,r,i,k)=(f,f',g,g')$ to obtain its specified sheaf isomorphism $\gamma:g_!f'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*g'_!$. In particular the map used is the open-adjunction transpose of restriction, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of the two sheaves.

source.place: Steps 3–4 repaired: the pro-etale degree-zero support comparison

proof.text:
The small-site module categories are Grothendieck, and every complex $M$ on $X'$ has a functorial K-injective resolution $M\to J$ with injective terms, by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Using the all-sheaf finite-CD bound from Step 1, apply [lem-exc-proetale-cartesian-open-injective-acyclic] to each $J^a$ to see that $g'_!J^a$ is $f_*$-acyclic. By exactness of open extension [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], $g'_!J$ represents $g'_!M$. Step 1's uniform bound and [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex] therefore identify $Rf_*g'_!M$ with $f_*g'_!J$. The definition of derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] computes $Rf'_*M$ by $f'_*J$. Exact $g_!$ and Step 2 now give
$$\Gamma_M:g_!Rf'_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*g'_!M.$$
Its representative is $g_!f'_*J\xrightarrow{\gamma_J}f_*g'_!J\to f_*I$ for a K-injective resolution $g'_!J\to I$. The natural acyclic-complex comparison in the cited finite-CD theorem makes this independent of resolutions and natural in $M$; it identifies the termwise maps of acyclic complexes with their derived maps.
To verify its open-adjunction normalization, restrict the chosen resolution $g'_!J\to I$ to $X'$. By [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction], $g'^*$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $g'_!$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $g'^*I$ K-injective. The induced map $J\to g'^*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives. Restricting direct image gives the degreewise identity $g^*f_*I=f'_*g'^*I$ by the section formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus the derived open-restriction isomorphism $\lambda_M:g^*Rf_*g'_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*M$ is inverse to the map computed by $f'_*J\to f'_*g'^*I$. Restriction of $\gamma_J$ in Step 2 is the identity under its specified $\lambda_J$, so restriction of the displayed representative of $\Gamma_M$ is exactly this map. Consequently $\lambda_M\circ g^*\Gamma_M=1$ under $g^*g_!\cong1$, and $\Gamma_M=\varepsilon_g\circ g_!(\lambda_M^{-1})$. The construction of this open-restriction isomorphism $\lambda$ uses no finite-CD bound or exceptional adjoint; it is available independently for the coefficient-class argument.

source.place: Steps 2–4 repaired: deriving the support comparison without using an etale triangle

proof.text:
For $M\in D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the open adjunctions [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the given proper adjunction [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and $\Gamma$ yield natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,g'^*Rf^\times K)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X}(g'_!M,Rf^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(Rf_*g'_!M,K)\\
&\xrightarrow{t\mapsto t\circ\Gamma_M}\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(g_!Rf'_*M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,g^*K).
\end{aligned}$$
These four bijections fix both the direction and normalization of the comparison.

Supply the right adjoint for $f'$ rather than assuming ambient data for it. Open localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] gives $g^*g_*N\cong N$ on module sheaves: after restriction to $Q\to Y'$, $(Y'\times_YQ)=Q$, with identical restriction maps and module actions. Choose a K-injective resolution using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Then [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] computes $Rg_*N$ by $g_*J$, so exact $g^*$ gives $g^*Rg_*N\cong N$ degreewise. Set $H=g'^*Rf^\times Rg_*$. Step 4 at $K=Rg_*N$, followed by this counit, gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,HN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,N).$$
Use [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to give $Rf'_*\dashv H$ its specified unit and counit, and choose this $H$ as $Rf'^\times$. This does not assert a FullCD/refinement datum for $f'$ over $S$.

source.place: Step 3 repaired: existence of the restricted right adjoint

proof.text: Compose Step 4 with $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns the resulting natural bijection of representable functors into an isomorphism $\beta_K:g'^*Rf^\times K\to Rf'^\times g^*K$: applying the same construction to the inverse bijection gives its inverse. To compute its actual map, evaluate at $M=g'^*Rf^\times K$ and $1_M$. The successive transposes in Step 4 are $\varepsilon_{g'}$, then $\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}$, then precomposition with $\Gamma_M$, and then the $g_!\dashv g^*$ transpose. The final transpose under $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$ is precisely the normalization in the statement, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Naturality of the Hom bijections proves naturality in $K$. Any other choice of right adjoint is identified by the same natural representables and hence has this comparison. This proves the arbitrary-open ambient assertion.

proof.text:
For the independent finite-field clause, $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only the ideals zero and one. The opens $X',Y'$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so $g,g'$ are quasi-compact and then finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. To check finite type over $k$ directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], take a finite affine cover of $Y$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras $B_i$ and finite affine covers of each inverse image in $Y'$ by finitely generated $B_i$-algebras $C_{ij}$. The union of the generators of $B_i$ over $k$ and $C_{ij}$ over $B_i$ generates $C_{ij}$ over $k$. Their finitely many affines cover $Y'$. Do this also for $X'$. Both proper compactifications $(\operatorname{id},f)$ and $(\operatorname{id},f')$ thus have finite-dimensional sources [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; use dimension bound zero on an empty source. Hence [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] applies to both proper maps.

Write a test object as $M\cong
u_{X'}^*M_0$, $M_0\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Exact comparison and open extension [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] allow termwise use of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], giving an etale-origin witness $g'_!M\cong
u_X^*g'^{\mathrm{et}}_!M_0$. Let $b_f:Rf_*
u_X^*\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and $b_{f'}$ be [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] at the proper compactifications, and let $e_g:
u_Y^*g^{\mathrm{et}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}g_!
u_{Y'}^*$, $e_{g'}$ be the open comparisons. All schemes are Noetherian, so [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] supplies $\Gamma^{\mathrm{et}}$. Define the bounded-class comparison by the explicit invertible composite
$$ egin{aligned}
g_!Rf'_*
u_{X'}^*M_0
&\xrightarrow{g_!b_{f'}}g_!
u_{Y'}^*Rf'_{\mathrm{et},*}M_0
\xrightarrow{e_g^{-1}}
u_Y^*g^{\mathrm{et}}_!Rf'_{\mathrm{et},*}M_0\
&\xrightarrow{
u_Y^*\Gamma^{\mathrm{et}}}
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}g'^{\mathrm{et}}_!M_0
\xrightarrow{b_f^{-1}}Rf_*
u_X^*g'^{\mathrm{et}}_!M_0
\xrightarrow{Rf_*e_{g'}}Rf_*g'_!
u_{X'}^*M_0.
\end{aligned}$$
For a witness $\alpha:
u_{X'}^*M_0	o M$, precompose by $g_!Rf'_*(\alpha^{-1})$ and postcompose by $Rf_*g'_!\alpha$. Full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts each morphism between witnesses uniquely; naturality of the displayed composite therefore proves independence of witness and naturality in $M$. This entire comparison uses etale-origin objects only.
The composite just specified has the required pro-etale open-adjunction normalization. Here is the comparison of maps. Properness gives the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] for $f,f'$. Its map $b_{u}:
u^*Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}	o Ru_*
u^*$ is the inverse of the notation $b_u$ used above, and it satisfies $\varepsilon_u^p\circ u_p^*b_u\circ a_u=
u^*\varepsilon_u^e$. The pullback comparisons $a_u$ commute with the Cartesian square by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The open-extension comparisons are their adjoint comparisons, as in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Apply the two pasting identities of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] first to these direct-image comparison squares and then to the two open adjunctions. They identify the open transpose of the five-arrow composite with the comparison pullback of the open transpose of $\Gamma^{\mathrm{et}}$; the displayed counit equation specifies each direct-image mate. By the Cartesian normalization in [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], that etale transpose is $(\lambda^{\mathrm{et}})^{-1}$. Thus, after the canonical pullback and direct-image identifications, the five-arrow composite $C_M$ satisfies $\lambda_M\circ g^*C_M=1$, with the open-restriction $\lambda_M$ constructed in Step 3. The sheaf/pullback section identifications apply to the same localized test objects, so this equation has the indicated pro-etale target. The open-adjunction bijection now gives $C_M=\varepsilon_g\circ g_!(\lambda_M^{-1})$. Therefore this relative-class comparison is the canonical proper/open map; when the optional datum holds it also agrees with Step 3's map on this class.

proof.text:
Choose $K\cong\nu_Y^*K_0$ with $K_0\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The comparison unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and formula [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] give $Rf^!K\cong\nu_X^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^\times K_0$. Open restriction commutes with $\nu^*$: on a pro-etale test object $T\to X'$ the section formula [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] gives $\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},(T\to X)_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ on both sides; the section pullbacks giving restriction maps and the constant-$A$ actions agree. Applying the same calculation to $Y'$ and then termwise using exactness [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives witnesses
$$B=g'^*Rf^!K\cong\nu_{X'}^*g'^{\mathrm{et},*}f_{\mathrm{et}}^\times K_0,\qquad
 C=Rf'^!g^*K\cong\nu_{X'}^*f'^{\times}_{\mathrm{et}}g^{\mathrm{et},*}K_0.$$
Here the etale adjoint values are bounded below, with the following check rather than an appeal to an unstated clause. The theorem [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] puts $\nu_X^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^\times K_0=Rf^!K$ in $D^+$. Exact comparison pullback commutes with cohomology [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. If an etale cohomology sheaf $F$ below this lower bound has $\nu_X^*F=0$, the unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] applied to $F[0]$ gives $F[0]\cong R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*(F[0])=0$, hence $F=0$. Thus $f_{\mathrm{et}}^\times K_0$ is bounded below. Applying these sentences with $X',Y',f',g^{\mathrm{et},*}K_0$ proves the bound for the other etale adjoint value. Exact restriction preserves both lower bounds. Thus both $B,C$ belong to the witnessed full category [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. For every object $M$ of this category, Step 7 gives an etale-origin witness for $g'_!M$ and its specified comparison $\Gamma_M$. The open adjunctions [prop-exc-open-adjoint] and relative adjunctions [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] yield
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,B)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X}(g'_!M,Rf^!K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(Rf_*g'_!M,K)\\
&\xrightarrow{t\mapsto t\circ\Gamma_M}\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(g_!Rf'_*M,K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,g^*K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,C).
\end{aligned}$$
Each relative adjunction has a bounded-below etale-origin source ($M$ or $g'_!M$) and bounded-below target ($g^*K$ or $K$). Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in this full category gives an isomorphism $B\to C$. Evaluating at $M=B$ and $1_B$ gives successively $\varepsilon_{g'}$, $\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}$, precomposition with $\Gamma_B$, its open transpose, and its relative proper transpose: this is exactly the displayed relative canonical comparison. This also proves naturality. An input sheaf in [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] supplies such a witness in degree zero, so this includes the source's coefficient-sheaf clause. No unrestricted ambient datum is inferred.
